analysis: Biomedical response coherently links cell biology, biochemistry, anatomy and physiology to pathology, immunity, pharmacology and biomedical research. The case-based disease course supports mechanisms, not supervised clinical training. The clear research and organ-system overlap is substantial even though medicine-specific placements and longitudinal skills remain absent.

Behavioural response uses cognition, language, social psychology, lifespan development, health psychology, psychopathology and psychological assessment to study behaviour and health, supported by sociology, qualitative inquiry and communication. The shared biomedical base grounds health questions. This is distinct from organ-system pathology and laboratory practice.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, evidence literacy, presentation and reflective development support the common foundation; this is distinct from longitudinal clinical professionalism.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: provides research design, sampling, experiments, surveys and inferential statistics for evaluating health evidence

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: teaches cleaning, manipulation and visualisation of research data, including a project; supplies a concrete data-handling foundation for biomedical and behavioural evidence

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: teaches virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism and reasoning about responsibility and equality, providing analytical frameworks for evaluating ethical health and research questions; it is not specialist medical ethics

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: examines institutions, race, gender and class through sociological theories, providing specific tools to investigate social differences in health and inclusion; healthcare teaching is not claimed

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: teaches qualitative inquiry into experience, meaning and power, supporting research on patient experience and healthcare interaction

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: teaches epidemiology, disease risk and critical evaluation of public-health evidence relevant to prevention and population-health promotion

HCBBIOM211.name: Functional Anatomy
HCBBIOM211.contribution: studies human anatomy and imaging as a biomedical foundation, but does not teach clinical examination or medical procedures

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: covers drug targets, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic effects and toxicity relevant to biomedical treatment knowledge, without clinical prescribing practice

HCBBIOM312.name: Infection & Immunity
HCBBIOM312.contribution: examines host–pathogen interaction and immunity, directly supporting biological understanding of infection and prevention

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.contribution: connects normal physiology to organ-system disease mechanisms and clinical cases, while remaining biomedical rather than clinical training

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: teaches comparative nervous-system biology, biorhythms, animal models, disorders and experimental laboratory methods; supplies neurobiological foundations without promising human clinical training

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: examines sensory processing and neural control of action using cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology, connecting nervous-system function to perception and functional impairment

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: examines memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, planning and decision-making, providing cognitive mechanisms for studying illness experience rather than training clinical interaction

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines speech production/comprehension, aphasia and dyslexia with experimental language neuroscience, providing a specific cognitive-function and impairment strand within the physical/mental-health concept

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: provides foundations in cells, molecules, genetics, microorganisms, organ systems and biomedical experimentation

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces brain and behaviour as a foundation for psychological aspects of health and care

HCBLIFE211.name: Molecular Cell Biology
HCBLIFE211.contribution: examines cell structure, gene expression, signalling and division as foundations for pathology

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: covers molecular, cellular and systems physiology of the human body as a medical foundation relevant to health

HCBLIFE213.name: Biochemistry
HCBLIFE213.contribution: covers biomolecules, metabolism and nucleic acids as biochemical foundations for physiology and disease

HCBLIFE214.name: Life Science Laboratory
HCBLIFE214.contribution: provides biochemical and molecular laboratory work, PCR, bioinformatics and interpretation of experimental results

HCBLIFE311.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
HCBLIFE311.contribution: covers cellular injury, inflammation, tissue repair, neoplasia and human molecular genetics relevant to disease mechanisms

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: examines attitudes, groups, interpersonal behaviour and social influence, supplying psychological mechanisms for studying health behaviour and responses to public messages

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: develops experimental design and multivariate statistics for health and behavioural research

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: examines mental disorders through biological, psychological, social and cultural mechanisms relevant to patient experience

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: examines biological, psychological and sociocultural influences on health, illness, behaviour and intervention

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: studies psychological assessment, psychodiagnostics, psychotherapy approaches and their ethics across the lifespan; this implements the mental-health direction but is not medical diagnostic training

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: develops systematic-review and meta-analytic methods for evidence-based health decisions

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: examines physical, cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan, including ageing

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: teaches framing, nudging, cognitive shorthands and ethics of public persuasion, supplying a method for analysing health-behaviour messages; its community project is not guaranteed to involve healthcare

academicConstruction: Screened current HCB and social science offerings and considered the third direction independently. Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation and Governance of Sustainability give useful general tools for environmental impact and institutions. Epidemiology and Medical & Health Psychology contribute health evidence. Their documented content does not integrate care delivery, procurement, clinical materials or organisational environmental impacts as a sustained sequence. This is a coherence finding, not an offering or timetable proxy. Psycholinguistics is available only in 2027h1 and follows the brain and behaviour gateway. Social Psychology moves to 2028h1, before Medical & Health Psychology. Perception & Action moves to 2029h1 after the neuroscience foundations. No course selections change.
